content: Aluminum hydroxide and magnesium hydroxide are antacids that are used together to alleviate symptoms such as heartburn, acid indigestion, and stomach upset. These medications may also be prescribed to manage symptoms in patients with conditions like peptic ulcers, gastritis, esophagitis, hiatal hernia, or excessive stomach acid (gastric hyperacidity). They work by combining with stomach acid and neutralizing it. These antacids are available over the counter without a prescription. In some cases, they may be prescribed for other uses; consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. This medication is available in the form of chewable tablets and liquid for oral use. Chew the tablets thoroughly before swallowing; do not swallow them whole. After taking the tablets, drink a full glass of water. If using the liquid form, shake the bottle well before each use to ensure the medicine is evenly mixed. The liquid can be mixed with water or milk if desired. Follow the instructions on the package label or your prescription label carefully, and ask your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take aluminum hydroxide and magnesium hydroxide antacids exactly as directed. Do not take more or less of the medication or take it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. Do not use antacids for more than 1–2 weeks unless instructed to do so by your doctor. Before taking aluminum hydroxide and magnesium hydroxide antacids, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to these medications or any other drugs. Provide a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, especially aspirin, cinoxacin (Cinobac), ciprofloxacin (Cipro), digoxin (Lanoxin), diazepam (Valium), enoxacin (Penetrex), ferrous sulfate (iron), fluconazole (Diflucan), indomethacin, isoniazid (INH), itraconazole (Sporanox), ketoconazole (Nizoral), levofloxacin (Levaquin), lomefloxacin (Maxaquin), nalidixic acid (NegGram), norfloxacin (Noroxin), ofloxacin (Floxin), sparfloxacin (Zagam), tetracycline (Achromycin, Sumycin), and vitamins. If your doctor advises you to take antacids while on these medications, do not take them within two hours of taking the antacid. Inform your doctor if you have or have ever had kidney disease. Additionally, let your doctor know if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. If you become pregnant while taking these antacids, contact your doctor immediately. If you are taking this medication for an ulcer, adhere strictly to the diet prescribed by your doctor. If you miss a scheduled dose of aluminum hydroxide and magnesium hydroxide, take the missed dose as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Side effects from aluminum hydroxide and magnesium hydroxide are uncommon. To avoid the chalky taste, take the medication with water or milk. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they are severe or persistent: diarrhea, constipation, loss of appetite, unusual tiredness, or muscle weakness. Store this medication in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or no longer needed medication. Consult your pharmacist for proper disposal instructions. If you are taking this medication under a doctor’s supervision, ensure you attend all scheduled appointments with your doctor. Do not share your medication with anyone else.
